title: Enough injectives and left exact invariants after an equivalence to discrete integer representations
statement: Let $G$ be a topological group in universe $u$, let $r=\max(u,s)$, and let $\mathcal A$ be any category with an equivalence $E:\mathcal A\simeq\operatorname{DiscreteRep}_{\mathbf Z}(G)$ [def-exc-discrete-modules-category], with representation carriers in universe $r$. Then $\mathcal A$ has enough injectives [def-sp-injective-resolutions], and the functor sending $M$ to the underlying additive group of $E(M)^G$ preserves finite limits [def-sp-left-exact-additive]. No compactness or abelian-category hypothesis on $\mathcal A$ is required.

source.place: Tag 04JF, functorial injective embeddings; Mathlib Rep.invariantsAdjunction and Adjunction.restrictFullyFaithful for left exactness

proof.text: Apply the arbitrary-ring functorial embedding theorem with R=Z and carrier universe max(u,s). For every M the component M to J(M) is monic and J(M) is injective. These give injective presentations; Mathlib EnoughInjectives.of_equivalence transports them along E.

The trivial representation on any integer module has open stabilizers because every stabilizer is the whole group. Lift the trivial-action functor to the full discrete subcategory. Restrict Rep.invariantsAdjunction along its fully faithful inclusion and the identity on integer modules, using Adjunction.restrictFullyFaithful. This makes the restricted invariants functor a right adjoint. Compose it with E and the underlying additive-group functor; all three preserve limits, so the composite preserves finite limits.
